license_declaration.product_identity_source: Paizo Pathfinder Roleplaying Game Bestiary, OGL §15 Product Identity section
license_declaration.product_identity_note: Per docs/governance/ogl-pi-blacklist.md §2.1's per-book override note: within Bestiary 1 itself, classic SRD monster species names (e.g. "Ankheg", "Dark Creeper") are presumptively Open Game Content, not Product Identity, matching the original d20 SRD's declaration -- this book's monster `name`/`id` fields are therefore classified OGL, not PI, unlike a non-bestiary context where a named creature could be PI. Named deities, unique NPCs, and unique places would still be Product Identity if present; none were found in this book's free-text `description` fields during this pass.

screening_method_note: This book's 164 records reached disk through TWO screening passes, and this note states both rather than implying one. PASS 1 -- cycle E2.0.9, 2026-07-27 -- covered the 45 records then on disk (41 monster + 4 equipment): a heuristic first-pass screen against a bounded, documented term list (the 20 canonical Golarion core deity names) run over every free-text `description` value in those records. The 41 monster records carry no free-text field at all -- only mechanical stat-block fields, verified by enumerating all data keys across all 41 monster/*.json -- so pass 1 had exactly 4 equipment `description` values to run over. PASS 2 covered the 119 records added on 2026-07-31 by `src/bin/ingest_races.rs` (11 race chassis + 108 standard racial traits): that binary runs a WIDER 54-term scan -- the same 20 deities plus 34 Golarion place and nation names -- over each record's `key`, `name` and `description`, and aborts the ingest with an error on any hit, so a record cannot reach disk unscreened. Zero matches were found in either pass. It is NOT an exhaustive human legal review, and no claim of exhaustive PI-freedom is made beyond: no substring match against the documented term lists was found.
